clue.text: Electronic sensor has nurse full of foreboding

indicators.note: the word for a nurse is filled up with the word for foreboding, which sits inside it

parts.note: a carer nurses someone
dread is a sense of foreboding

explanation.surface: A spooky nurse with a gadget that picks up her sense of impending doom.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that reads the chip or stripe on a payment card is an electronic sensing unit.

clue.text: Carol's first partner, plump

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name Carol is wanted here

parts.note: hubby is an informal word for a husband, a partner

explanation.surface: Carol's first husband is described as rather plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby and plump are synonyms for a pleasantly rounded, slightly fat figure.

clue.text: Massive memorial overlooking a lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a monument is a memorial
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A huge memorial built on a hill above a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Monumental means on a huge scale, so it is a synonym of massive.

clue.text: Armada with no time to escape

indicators.note: having no time means the letter for time is dropped from the fleet word

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships

explanation.surface: The Spanish Armada had no time left to get away.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away, a direct synonym of escape as a verb.

clue.text: Sort on pitch always given similar roles?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
to pitch something is to throw or cast it

explanation.surface: An actor who always plays the same part, perhaps sorted by the pitch of their voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A typecast actor is repeatedly chosen for the same kind of part; the question mark flags the descriptive definition.

clue.text: Chatter about right clothing

indicators.note: the word for chatter goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: gab is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Gossip about the right thing to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothes or dress, especially of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Actor, drama queen?

parts.note: a play is a drama
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A theatrical performer who is something of a drama queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama queen' reads as a single phrase but splits into its two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage, an old synonym for an actor.

clue.text: Round fired by every gun in wood — screech heard, exposing game

indicators.note: heard tells us the pieces are spoken, so we enter words that sound like them

parts.words: Round fired by every gun in wood — screech
parts.note: a volley is a round fired by every gun at once; set in, after, the wood, beech; a screech is a bawl, giving BEECH VOLLEY BAWL

explanation.surface: A battle scene in a forest: a volley of gunfire and screaming, with a game being exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' works on the run: BEECH sounds like BEACH and BAWL like BALL, while VOLLEY is unchanged when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Beach volleyball is a sport played on sand, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Deliveries, unusually large close to Christmas

parts.note: a bumper crop or edition is an unusually large one

indicators.note: the close, end, of the word Christmas gives its last letter

explanation.surface: Huge parcel deliveries arriving just before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bumper is a short-pitched ball that rears up at the batsman; deliveries are balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumpers are short-pitched balls in cricket, an example of deliveries from a bowler.

clue.text: Mother and daughter, very angry

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: Mother and daughter are both furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in its informal sense means furious, a synonym of very angry.

clue.text: Favourite student — young Frank Sinatra, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a teacher's pet, someone in special favour
Sinatra was nicknamed Ol' Blue Eyes, so as a youth he was literally a lad with blue eyes

explanation.surface: A teacher's pet who looks like the young Sinatra.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-eyed boy is a favourite who can do no wrong; Sinatra, famous for blue eyes, fits literally.

clue.text: Poem in English on ending of slavery

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the ending of the word slavery is its final letter

explanation.surface: A poem in English about the end of slavery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' = LEG comes from cricket, where the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, typically a lament for the dead, so it is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Rearrange an overdue attempt

indicators.note: an instruction to put the following letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A command to reschedule a long-delayed try.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an earnest try or effort, a synonym of attempt as a noun.

clue.text: Court order: one in residence affected

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so these letters are changed in order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A court order that affects one person living at a particular address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' mixes RESIDENCE into DECREENIS; I, one, sits in the answer beside it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is a provisional order of divorce made by a court.

clue.text: How goods may be dispatched in van poor pal damaged

indicators.note: damaged suggests something broken up, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Goods are sent out in a battered van with a poor friend driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sent on approval may be returned if the buyer is not satisfied, a way of sending them.

clue.text: Team overcome, losing a wager

parts.note: a side is a team

indicators.note: losing means the letter A is dropped from the word for overcome

parts.note: to beat is to overcome

explanation.surface: A team is beaten and loses money on a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A side bet is an extra wager placed alongside the main one, so it is a kind of wager.

clue.text: Rest of British more readily accepting lead from Europe

indicators.note: the word for more readily takes in, accepts, the letter from Europe

parts.note: rather means more willingly, more readily

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The British are happier to take a break when Europe leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short pause for rest, so it means rest as a noun.

clue.text: Old sailor's weapon nicked by young woman

parts.note: nicked here means cut slightly, not stolen
a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A pirate's sword stolen by a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' suggests stolen (British slang) but here means given a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once used by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Odd stone on practice area

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight of fourteen pounds
a range is an area for practice, as a driving or firing range

explanation.surface: A strange stone found lying on a golf practice ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and odd are synonyms for unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: French football club, Reims, all upset about base

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the letter for base
upset means overturned, so these letters are tumbled into a new arrangement

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: Reims supporters upset about a rival club's base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' mixes REIMS and ALL; 'about' puts that mix around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympique de Marseille is a leading French football club named after its city.

clue.text: Young lady, not entirely suitable — a square peg in a round hole, maybe

definitions.text: a square peg in a round hole, maybe

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman
fit means suitable, as in fit for purpose

explanation.surface: A girl who does not quite fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: A square peg in a round hole is an idiom for someone out of place, a person who does not belong.

clue.text: Marvellous agent, American, returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A wonderful American secret agent comes home.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal word for excellent or wonderful, a synonym of marvellous.

clue.text: Guide's phrase in need of translation

indicators.note: a phrase needing translation must be turned into something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tour guide's expression that a foreigner must have translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide's' is Guide is, with the apostrophe s as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famous for serving as mountain guides on climbing expeditions.

clue.text: Do brief amendment

parts.note: short means brief
a change is an amendment

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a quick revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the informal verb meaning to cheat, not the everyday verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, as when giving too little money back in a transaction.

clue.text: Swear-word used in set-to at home

indicators.note: the letters used in the phrase are found within it, running across the words

explanation.surface: Bad language heard during a domestic row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear-word' looks like a curse but means a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a sworn promise, a word one swears, though it can also mean a curse.

clue.text: Natural successor, that woman touring India

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the pronoun surrounds the letter for India

parts.note: her is the pronoun for that woman
India is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for I

explanation.surface: A woman travelling around India is the obvious successor.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who will inherit by birth, a natural successor to an estate or title.

clue.text: Have nothing with last of gin

parts.note: O is the round shape of zero, nothing

indicators.note: the last letter of the word gin is wanted

explanation.surface: Having nothing but the last drop of gin.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, a synonym of have in its sense of possess.

clue.text: Before anything else, see leading article inside

parts.note: in means inside
the is the definite article
first means leading, ahead of the rest
a see is a bishop's seat or place

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at the main newspaper article within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading article' suggests a newspaper editorial but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means firstly or to begin with, so it introduces what comes before anything else.
